segments.arabic: [515] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج حين زاغت الشمس فصلى الظهر فقام على المنبر فذكر الساعة فذكر أن فيها أمورا عظاما، ثم قال من أحب أن يسأل عن شيء فليسأل فلا تسألوني عن شيء إلا أخبرتكم ما دمت في مقامي هذا فأكثر الناس في البكاء وأكثر أن يقول سلوني فقام عبد الله بن حذافة السهمي، فقال من أبي قال أبوك حذافة ثم أكثر أن يقول سلوني فبرك عمر على ركبتيه، فقال رضينا بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا وبمحمد نبيا فسكت، ثم قال عرضت علي الجنة والنار آنفا في عرض هذا الحائط فلم أر كالخير والشر
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out when the sun had begun to decline and prayed Dhuhr. He stood on the pulpit and mentioned the Hour, saying that it would contain momentous events. Then he said: “Whoever wishes to ask about something, let him ask. You will not ask me about anything without my telling you, as long as I remain in this place.” The people wept a great deal, and he repeatedly said: “Ask me.” ‘Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi stood up and said: “Who is my father?” He said: “Your father is Hudhafah.” Then he repeatedly said: “Ask me.” ‘Umar knelt on his knees and said: “We are content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as Prophet.” He fell silent, then said: “The Garden and the Fire were shown to me just now across this wall. I have never seen the like of that good and evil.”

notes: The complete question-and-answer sequence, both repeated invitations to ask, Umar’s kneeling and the pause before the final statement remain. No event details or names absent from the selected report are added. The full Abu al-Yaman–Shuayb–al-Zuhri–Anas chain remains.

The working rendering takes أكثر الناس في البكاء as extensive weeping by the people, without changing it to an explicit numerical majority. The final comparison retains both good and evil; the wall description does not add a screen or a physical opening. Across is provisional for في عرض and needs independent lexical review.

segments.arabic: [516] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي المنهال عن أبي برزة
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Barzah:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي الصبح وأحدنا يعرف جليسه ويقرأ فيها ما بين الستين إلى المائة ويصلي الظهر إذا زالت الشمس والعصر وأحدنا يذهب إلى أقصى المدينة ثم يرجع والشمس حية
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Subh when one of us could recognize the person sitting beside him, and he would recite between sixty and a hundred in it. He prayed Dhuhr when the sun had declined, and ‘Asr when one of us could go to the farthest part of Madinah and return while the sun was still bright.

segments.arabic: ونسيت ما قال في المغرب
segments.english: And I forgot what he said about Maghrib.

segments.arabic: ولا نبالي بتأخير العشاء إلى ثلث الليل، ثم قال إلى شطر الليل،
segments.english: And we did not mind delaying ‘Isha’ until a third of the night. Then he said: “Until half of the night.”

segments.arabic: وقال معاذ قال شعبة ثم لقيته مرة، فقال أو ثلث الليل
segments.english: And Mu‘adh said: Shu‘bah said: Then I met him on one occasion, and he said: “Or a third of the night.”

notes: The selected first-person we in ولا نبالي is retained, rather than replacing it with the English comparisons’ he. The initial third, subsequent half, and closing or a third remain in their original order. Muadh’s attribution is retained; the Khan-family comparison omits this closing transmission.

The Arabic leaves the counted item after sixty to a hundred implicit; no parenthetical Quranic verses is inserted. Bright is provisional for حية: Bewley uses white and Khan uses hot. The working rendering does not add a clock time, sunset interval, or the comparisons’ after-prayer gloss. The forgetfulness statement remains a separately marked narrator remark.

segments.arabic: [517] حدثنا محمد يعني ابن مقاتل قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا خالد بن عبد الرحمن حدثني غالب القطان عن بكر بن عبد الله المزني عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Muqatil—related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed us: Ghalib al-Qattan related to me, from Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا إذا صلينا خلف رسول الله ﷺ بالظهائر فسجدنا على ثيابنا اتقاء الحر
segments.english: When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at midday, we prostrated on our clothing to protect ourselves from the heat.

notes: The full chain keeps Muhammad’s meaning-Ibn-Muqatil clarification and the related-to-me form after Khalid’s informed-us. The selected فسجدنا includes a connecting fa not present in the inspected modern print’s سجدنا; it is retained without silently editing the source.

The selected plural بالظهائر is rendered at midday. The English comparisons name Dhuhr; no prayer name absent from this report is inserted. Clothing and protection from heat remain without adding a specific body part or surface.

segments.arabic: [518] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد هو ابن زيد عن عمرو بن دينار عن جابر بن زيد عن ابن عباس
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad—he is Ibn Zayd—related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى بالمدينة سبعا وثمانيا الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء،
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed seven and eight in Madinah: Dhuhr and ‘Asr, and Maghrib and ‘Isha’.

segments.arabic: فقال أيوب لعله في ليلة مطيرة قال عسى
segments.english: Ayyub said: “Perhaps it was on a rainy night.” He said: “Perhaps.”

notes: The selected order seven and eight and the following prayer-name order are both retained. The working text does not add respectively or silently rearrange the numbers. The selected Arabic leaves the counted units implicit.

The last speaker is not named in the selected Arabic or either inspected print. Both inspected English comparisons supply Anas, which is not imported. The rainy-night suggestion remains singular and explicitly tentative; it is not converted into a reason stated by the Prophet.

segments.arabic: [519] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا أنس بن عياض عن هشام عن أبيه أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from Hisham, from his father, that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي العصر والشمس لم تخرج من حجرتها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sunlight had not yet left her chamber.

notes: The selected third-person her chamber is retained rather than converting it to the Khan-family comparison’s my chamber. Hisham’s father is not expanded to a name absent from this chain.

This remains a distinct numbered report from 520 and 521. The modern print places Abu Usamah’s alternative chamber wording at the chapter heading; the selected digital source and historical print retain that transmission after the next report. It is preserved once at its selected location in 520.

segments.arabic: [520] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا الليث عن ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ صلى العصر والشمس في حجرتها لم يظهر الفيء من حجرتها،
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Asr while the sunlight was in her chamber and the shade had not yet spread in her chamber.

segments.arabic: وقال أبو أسامة عن هشام من قعر حجرتها
segments.english: And Abu Usamah said, from Hisham: “From the inner part of her chamber.”

notes: The Abu Usamah–Hisham wording is present after this report in the selected digital paragraph and the historical print. The modern print places it with the chapter heading before 544. Bewley places a shortened Hisham clause in the chapter context, and the Khan-family comparison omits it. Its selected location and complete attribution are retained.

Ibn Hajar distinguishes sunlight leaving the chamber from shade spreading in it. The working rendering of لم يظهر الفيء من حجرتها follows that spatial explanation and the English comparisons’ in-the-chamber sense, without importing room dimensions or an exact time. The retained preposition من and the lexical choice spread require independent review. The closing قعر is rendered inner part without adding an implied verb.

segments.arabic: [521] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: أخبرنا ابن عيينة عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي صلاة العصر والشمس طالعة في حجرتي لم يظهر الفيء بعد،
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the ‘Asr prayer while the sunlight was shining in my chamber and the shade had not yet appeared.

segments.arabic: وقال: مالك ويحيى بن سعيد وشعيب وابن أبي حفصة والشمس قبل أن تظهر
segments.english: And Malik, Yahya ibn Sa‘id, Shu‘ayb and Ibn Abi Hafsah said: “And the sunlight, before it rose out.”

notes: The selected first-person my chamber stays distinct from her chamber in 519–520. All four closing transmitters remain, although the Khan-family comparison omits the closing wording.

The final قبل أن تظهر is a fragment with its own attribution, not an extra clause silently joined to Aisha’s first sentence. Ibn Hajar explains the sunlight’s appearance here as rising out of the chamber; the working wording retains that sense and does not add the chamber noun absent from this closing fragment. Independent lexical review remains pending.

segments.arabic: [522] حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا عوف عن سيار بن سلامة قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: ‘Awf informed us, from Sayyar ibn Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: دخلت أنا وأبي على أبي برزة الأسلمي، فقال له أبي كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي المكتوبة، فقال: كان يصلي الهجير التي تدعونها الأولى حين تدحض الشمس ويصلي العصر ثم يرجع أحدنا إلى رحله في أقصى المدينة والشمس حية
segments.english: My father and I went in to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father asked him: “How did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray the obligatory prayer?” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer, which you call the first, when the sun declined. He prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his dwelling in the farthest part of Madinah while the sun was still bright.”

segments.arabic: ونسيت ما قال في المغرب
segments.english: And I forgot what he said about Maghrib.

segments.arabic: وكان يستحب أن يؤخر العشاء التي تدعونها العتمة وكان يكره النوم قبلها والحديث بعدها وكان ينفتل من صلاة الغداة حين يعرف الرجل جليسه ويقرأ بالستين إلى المائة
segments.english: And he preferred to delay ‘Isha’, which you call al-‘Atamah. He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He would turn away from the morning prayer when a man could recognize the person sitting beside him, and he would recite sixty to a hundred.

notes: The complete father-and-son frame, alternative prayer names, narrator’s forgetfulness, sleep/conversation sequence and morning ending remain. The Arabic’s reported question does not explicitly add five or congregational, so the Khan-family comparison’s additions are not imported.

Bright provisionally renders حية without adding a temperature or fixed interval. The counted object after sixty to a hundred remains implicit as in the Arabic, and the morning departure is not converted into an exact sunrise time. The narrator remark is visibly separate from the surrounding account.

segments.arabic: [523] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا نصلي العصر ثم يخرج الإنسان إلى بني عمرو بن عوف فيجدهم يصلون العصر
segments.english: We used to pray ‘Asr. Then a person would go out to Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and find them praying ‘Asr.

notes: The full Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah chain is retained. The destination is the named Banu Amr ibn Awf; no distance, village location or judgement about their prayer is added.

segments.arabic: [524] حدثنا ابن مقاتل قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا أبو بكر ابن عثمان بن سهل بن حنيف قال: سمعت أبا أمامة يقول
segments.english: Ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Uthman ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf informed us. He said: I heard Abu Umamah say:

segments.arabic: صلينا مع عمر بن عبد العزيز الظهر ثم خرجنا حتى دخلنا على أنس بن مالك فوجدناه يصلي العصر فقلت: يا عم ما هذه الصلاة التي صليت قال العصر وهذه صلاة رسول الله ﷺ التي كنا نصلي معه
segments.english: We prayed Dhuhr with ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz. Then we went out until we came in to Anas ibn Malik, and found him praying ‘Asr. I said: “Uncle, what is this prayer that you prayed?” He said: “‘Asr. And this is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which we used to pray with him.”

notes: The unexpanded opening Ibn Muqatil, full Abu Bakr name, I-heard formula and Abu Umamah’s statement remain. Uncle is retained as the form of address without asserting a biological relationship. The closing clause does not add the time of from the Khan-family parentheses.

segments.arabic: [525] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني أنس بن مالك قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to me. He said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي العصر والشمس مرتفعة حية فيذهب الذاهب إلى العوالي فيأتيهم والشمس مرتفعة وبعض العوالي من المدينة على أربعة أميال أو نحوه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sun was high and bright. A person would go to al-‘Awali and reach them while the sun was still high. Some of al-‘Awali are four miles from Madinah, or thereabouts.

notes: The selected digital source and modern print place this report before the Quba report at 526; the historical print reverses those two reports. Individual chain/body matching, not page order alone, establishes each comparison. The selected order is retained.

The distance qualifier or thereabouts and the distinct high/bright words remain. No modern kilometre conversion, universal distance for every settlement, or clock-time calculation is inserted. Bright is a provisional rendering of حية, alongside the English comparisons’ white/hot.

segments.arabic: [526] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا نصلي العصر ثم يذهب الذاهب منا إلى قباء فيأتيهم والشمس مرتفعة
segments.english: We used to pray ‘Asr. Then one of us would go to Quba’ and reach them while the sun was still high.

notes: The Quba destination is retained as its own report, not merged with the preceding al-Awali report. The selected and modern order differs from the historical print’s placement; the full chain and body were matched individually. No distance is borrowed from 525.

segments.arabic: [527] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الذي تفوته صلاة العصر كأنما وتر أهله وماله
segments.english: “The one who misses the ‘Asr prayer is as though he has been deprived of his family and his wealth.”

notes: The selected wording says misses and contains no intentionally qualification. The English comparison’s parenthetical qualification is not inserted. The distinct verb ترك in the following report is not used to collapse the two reports into one.

The historical print follows the report with Abu Abd Allah’s separate lexical remark on وتر, absent from the selected digital paragraph and the inspected modern page. This edition difference is recorded without adding that single-witness material to the selected report.

segments.arabic: [528] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير عن أبي قلابة عن أبي المليح قال
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Malih, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا مع بريدة في غزوة في يوم ذي غيم، فقال بكروا بصلاة العصر فإن النبي ﷺ قال: من ترك صلاة العصر فقد حبط عمله
segments.english: We were with Buraydah on an expedition on a cloudy day. He said: “Pray ‘Asr early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

notes: The expedition, cloudy day, instruction from Buraydah and embedded Prophetic statement remain distinct. The selected singular عمله is rendered his work; the Khan-family all and parenthetical good are not added. No legal ruling or explanation of the scope of nullification is inserted into the quotation.

segments.arabic: [529] حدثنا الحميدي قال: حدثنا مروان بن معاوية قال: حدثنا إسماعيل عن قيس عن جرير قال
segments.english: Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Qays, from Jarir, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا عند النبي ﷺ فنظر إلى القمر ليلة يعني البدر، فقال إنكم سترون ربكم كما ترون هذا القمر لا تضامون في رؤيته فإن استطعتم أن لا تغلبوا على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها فافعلوا ثم قرأ { وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب }
segments.english: We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon one night—meaning the full moon—and said: “You will indeed see your Lord as you see this moon, without suffering harm in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome and missing a prayer before the sun rises and before it sets, then do so.” Then he recited: “And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting.”

segments.arabic: قال إسماعيل افعلوا لا تفوتنكم
segments.english: Isma‘il said: “Do so; do not let it escape you.”

notes: The selected Jarir name remains unexpanded; the historical print names Jarir ibn Abd Allah. The parenthetical meaning-the-full-moon phrase, complete selected Quranic fragment and Ismail’s closing wording remain. No Fajr/Asr labels, sleep/business gloss, or unstated cause of missing prayer is added.

Ibn Hajar records the light-mim reading of لا تضامون as absence of harm and a doubled-mim reading concerning crowding. The working rendering follows the former; the unvowelled digital Arabic is not silently vocalized or changed. This lexical decision remains provisional. The final لا تفوتنكم remains a singular pronoun in English rather than inserting two prayers.

segments.arabic: [530] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار ويجتمعون في صلاة الفجر وصلاة العصر ثم يعرج الذين باتوا فيكم فيسألهم وهو أعلم بهم كيف تركتم عبادي فيقولون تركناهم وهم يصلون وأتيناهم وهم يصلون
segments.english: “Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the ‘Asr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—though He knows them better—‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say: ‘We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’”

notes: The selected related-to-us form for Malik matches the inspected modern print; the historical print has informed-us. The selected reporting verb is retained. Both groups of angels and both named prayers remain, with no added destination for the ascent.

The selected Arabic leaves the subject of asks as a pronoun, so the working translation uses He without inserting an absent name. The parenthetical وهو أعلم بهم remains He knows them better, without replacing them with you. Ibn Hajar notes the omitted explicit questioner in the majority of Malik narrations. The response keeps leaving before coming, as selected, rather than reordering the two clauses.
